decision: Lead with the outcome, then show how. Savar, 2026-11-11: 'Every kid is gonna do five days a week ... We predict Leah can reach x level by x date. And then we have to show how. We gotta lead with the outcome.'
invariants: one pace: 5 days a week, no pace switch
the first line is 'We predict [name] can reach a [Grade N] level by [Month Year]'
pages a day and minutes from D-186
dates from the real level book counts, a book every 2 weeks
no level ids shown to a parent
primary_axis: how the 'how' is shown: a route by grade (N), numbered steps under a prediction card (O), today and the goal side by side plus what Unica does (P)

options.bet: Big sentence with the date highlighted, the plan in four numbers, then one column per grade on a time track
options.benefit: Typographic, calm, the route and its topics in one view
options.cost: Columns get narrow when a stage is short
options.risk: Reads as an editorial page, not a product card

options.bet: One warm card: sentence, plan chips, a clean curve to a dated flag; numbered steps under it
options.benefit: The most 'product' look; the curve shows the climb at a glance
options.cost: A chart in the email must be an image
options.risk: The curve shape is a drawing, not data between the grade points

options.bet: Real math today beside real math at the goal, then three steps: a workbook every 2 weeks, 8 pages a day, every page marked
options.benefit: A parent can picture the result and sees how Unica does it
options.cost: Example problems must come from real question templates
options.risk: One problem stands for a whole grade
